WU-002.title: Add merge_lock and state_lock parameters to execute_wu()
WU-002.description: Extend execute_wu() to accept two asyncio.Lock arguments. Wrap the merge_branch() call with `async with merge_lock`. Replace every write_state() site with the acquire→reread→mutate→write pattern using state_lock. There are four write sites: (1) set in_progress at the top, (2) commit verdict in the try block, (3) AgentHaltError handler, (4) bare Exception handler. Sites 3 and 4 already re-read state before writing; add the lock around each. Site 1 and 2 require a fresh read_state() inside the lock so the local `state`/`wu_state` refs are not stale. Re-derive failure_count from the freshly read state inside the verdict lock block.
acceptance_criteria: execute_wu() signature is: async def execute_wu(wu, session_manager, target_repo, context_md, *, merge_lock: asyncio.Lock, state_lock: asyncio.Lock) -> str
merge_branch() is called only while merge_lock is held
All four write_state() call sites acquire state_lock, call read_state() to get a fresh snapshot, apply only this WU's changes to that snapshot, then call write_state()
failure_count is read from the fresh state snapshot inside the verdict lock block, not from the stale top-of-function snapshot
Return type is unchanged (str verdict: 'pass', 'fail', or 'reshape')
The existing except Exception guard still swallows all errors and returns 'fail'

last_review.summary: White-Hat: All six ACs are satisfied. The signature is keyword-only with correct type annotations (line 237–245). merge_branch() has exactly one call site and it is wrapped in `async with merge_lock` (lines 285–286). All four write_state() sites follow the acquire→read_state()→mutate→write_state() pattern (sites 1/2/3/4 at lines 259–262, 290–313, 322–328, 333–338). failure_count is re-derived from the freshly read wu_state inside the verdict lock (line 293), not from the stale top-of-function snapshot; the earlier bare read at line 275 is correctly scoped to reviewer-context only and is explicitly commented as such. Return type annotation is `-> str` and all return paths yield 'pass', 'fail', or 'reshape'. The bare `except Exception` guard (lines 331–339) still swallows all errors and returns 'fail'. Black-Hat: (1) If merge_branch() raises, the context manager releases merge_lock cleanly and the exception falls through to the bare Exception handler, which marks status='failed' — correct. (2) The worktree finally-block (lines 341–343) always executes, preventing orphaned worktrees. (3) The batch_number write in run_batch() (lines 413–415) bypasses state_lock, but it occurs before the concurrent execution loop and is a known Phase-2-only pattern — not a defect against this WU's scope. (4) mark_downstream_blocked() is called inside the state_lock at every reshape/pivot path, which is correct since it mutates the freshly acquired state snapshot. No edge-case holes found that fall within this WU's scope. Domain: Only src/overture/batch_manager.py was modified; run_batch() update is justified as the direct caller that must create and forward the new locks.

file_feedback.notes: execute_wu() signature, all four state_lock sites, the merge_lock wrapping, and failure_count re-derivation are all correct. run_batch() cleanly instantiates both locks before the WU loop and forwards them as keyword arguments, keeping the call site forward-compatible with the Phase-3 TaskGroup refactor described in the module docstring.

WU-003.title: Refactor run_batch() to use asyncio.TaskGroup for parallel WU execution
WU-003.description: Replace the sequential `for wu in batch` loop in run_batch() with asyncio.TaskGroup. Create merge_lock and state_lock as asyncio.Lock instances at the top of the function and pass them to every execute_wu() call. Collect verdicts into a dict keyed by wu_id using a closure or a shared results dict populated by each task coroutine. After the TaskGroup block closes (all tasks complete), iterate results to build the summary dict and print per-WU verdicts. Remove the per-iteration `needs_user_pivot` break — the orchestrator handles pivot detection after run_batch() returns. The summary dict shape {ready, passed, failed, reshaped} and the function's external signature are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: run_batch() creates merge_lock = asyncio.Lock() and state_lock = asyncio.Lock() before the TaskGroup
All WUs in the batch are launched as tasks inside a single `async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:` block
Each task receives merge_lock and state_lock
The sequential `for wu in batch` loop is removed
Verdicts are collected after the TaskGroup closes and used to compute the summary dict
The function returns the same {ready, passed, failed, reshaped} dict
No sibling task is cancelled when a WU sets needs_user_pivot

last_review.summary: White-Hat: All 7 ACs are satisfied. merge_lock and state_lock are created as asyncio.Lock() instances at lines 417–418, before the TaskGroup. All WUs are launched inside a single `async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:` block (line 430), each task receiving both locks via the _run_one closure that calls execute_wu(). The old sequential for-loop is gone — replaced by parallel task creation. Verdicts flow into the results dict after the TaskGroup closes (line 435+), and the summary dict preserves the {ready, passed, failed, reshaped} shape exactly. The needs_user_pivot flag is set inside execute_wu() as a state field and execute_wu() returns 'fail' (never raises), so no TaskGroup-level cancellation of siblings occurs. Black-Hat: (1) The results dict is written by coroutines without a lock, but asyncio's single-threaded cooperative model makes this safe — no actual data race. (2) batch_number is written to state before TaskGroup launch (line 413), outside state_lock, but this is safe since no tasks are running yet. (3) _run_reviewer() receives failure_count as a keyword argument but the _REVIEWER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE has no {failure_count} placeholder — the kwarg is silently ignored by str.format(); harmless but dead code. (4) The general except Exception in execute_wu() swallows all errors and returns 'fail', which prevents any TaskGroup sibling cancellation — this is correct and intentional per AC7. Domain: pyproject.toml (pytest-asyncio test dep), tests/__init__.py (package init), and tests/test_batch_manager.py are all touched. The WU explicitly required parallel execution with locks and the test infrastructure is mandatory to validate concurrency behaviour; these breaches are justified. The implementer's domain breach justification references 'AC8' which does not exist in this WU — the correct justification is that the WU description and ACs implicitly require tests to validate the TaskGroup pattern. This is a documentation inaccuracy in the report only, not a code defect.

file_feedback.notes: run_batch() is clean and correct. merge_lock and state_lock are scoped appropriately. The re-read-from-disk pattern inside state_lock is correctly applied at every write site in execute_wu(). The _run_one closure correctly captures wu_id to avoid loop-variable aliasing. The finally block guarantees worktree cleanup even on agent errors. Minor nit: failure_count is passed as a kwarg to _run_reviewer() but is not consumed by the template — dead parameter that should be removed in a follow-up, but not a correctness issue.

Covers select_batch() thoroughly (no overlap, overlap skip, max size cap, empty domain). test_run_batch_parallel exercises the real TaskGroup path with stubbed execute_wu() and validates state consistency across concurrent writes. test_execute_wu_passes_locks uses a TrackingLock subclass to assert both state_lock (≥2 acquisitions: in_progress write + final write) and merge_lock (exactly 1 acquisition) are used correctly. Solid coverage.
pytest-asyncio added to [project.optional-dependencies].test and asyncio_mode = 'auto' set in [tool.pytest.ini_options]. Correct and necessary.
Empty init, required for pytest package collection. No concerns.

WU-004.title: Write unit tests for select_batch() — no-overlap and overlap cases
WU-004.description: Create tests/test_batch_manager.py with two synchronous pytest test functions covering the select_batch() domain-overlap logic. No mocking required — select_batch() is a pure function. Tests must not import from orchestrator, planner, or gatherer to keep them dependency-light.

No direct imports from orchestrator, planner, or gatherer in the test file. Black-Hat: the transitive import of planner/sdk_wrapper through batch_manager is a pre-existing coupling and carries no runtime risk in a properly installed venv. Edge cases (empty input, WU with no domain) are not in scope and the function handles them gracefully. The lone domain breach — tests/__init__.py — is fully justified as a required package marker for the pytest invocation demanded by AC-4.

file_feedback.notes: All three test functions are logically correct and directly traceable to their respective ACs. The _make_wu helper keeps fixture construction DRY. Assertions are precise (exact len check + per-ID membership checks). The overlap test correctly relies on list order to make the first-seen priority deterministic.
